name: comfort
description: Being within a tolerable zone of physical, social, or mental discomfort.
perceptions: There's nothing annoying me physically, no unusual anxiety, no particular social pressures.

variations.name: social comfort
variations.description: The feeling that you're amongst people who accept an important part of your identity.
perceptions: I'm amongst people who respect and accept me as part of the group.
I don't have to strive for acceptance.

variations.name: physical comfort
variations.description: A perception that your body is not experiencing significant discomfort. In the modern world, we tend to take comfort for granted.
perceptions: I'm healthy, it's not too hot, not too cold, the chair is comfy, all is well.

variations.name: mental comfort
variations.description: A perception that your mind is not experiencing significant discomfort or strong desires.
perceptions: I'm not particularly anxious about anything.
I'm doing things that are aligned with my goals and preferences.
examples: doing a favorite puzzle to kill time

commentaries.quote: 'Comfort' is relative. Most of us are never truly without some kind of discomfort for long, but some people have higher tolerances physical or social discomfort.
You can be physically comfortable while being mentally uncomfortable or vice versa. In fact, for many of us in the modern world, they're almost always out of sync by definition.
Art should comfort the disturbed and disturb the comfortable.
We find comfort among those who agree with us - growth among those who don't.
